owner_fcf_base: Owner FCF base = FY2025 reported FCF $498.3M minus 100% of SBC $13.8M = $484.5M (owner-FCF margin ~60.7% on $798.2M revenue). SBC is treated as a cash expense per owner-earnings discipline; impact is small here since SBC is only 2.77% of FCF / 1.73% of revenue — among the lowest in the QG universe.

assumptions.sbc_treatment: 100% of SBC ($13.8M) deducted from reported FCF as a cash expense to derive owner earnings ($484.5M base). SBC is immaterial (1.73% of revenue, 2.77% of FCF).

conservador.note: Sostained oil-price softness and slower royalty/production growth. Owner-FCF grows ~8% CAGR in years 1-5, decelerating from 6% to 3% in years 6-10; terminal g 2.5%. Water segment grows but data-center/surface-monetization optionality stays muted. Yr10 owner FCF ~$887M. IV ~$166.

base.note: Consistent with track record (FY2025 revenue +29% organic / +29% royalty production, Q1-26 +21% YoY, ~62% FCF margin, ROIC ~43%). Owner-FCF ~13% CAGR years 1-5, declining 9%->4% years 6-10; terminal g 3.0%. Royalty volume growth + water expansion + modest land/data-center monetization. Yr10 owner FCF ~$1.22B. IV ~$231 — still ~36% below the $361 price, confirming a rich multiple (~51x owner FCF).

optimista.note: Perfect execution: ~18% owner-FCF CAGR years 1-5 on continued Permian royalty volume growth, scaled water/produced-water business, and material surface/data-center land monetization (e.g. the Q1-26 $42.5M financing arrangement as a template). Declines 12%->5% years 6-10; terminal g 3.5%. Yr10 owner FCF ~$1.67B. IV ~$325 — approaches but still below the current price.

sanity_check: Shareholder-return contrast (not used in valuation): regular dividend $2.40/yr = ~0.66% yield at $361.11; TPL also pays special dividends and runs opportunistic buybacks, but total shareholder yield remains low (~1-2%) because the stock trades at a very high multiple. Owner-FCF yield on price is only ~1.94% (~51x price/owner-FCF), versus a ~62% reported FCF margin and net-cash balance sheet — the premium reflects scarcity, royalty quality and optionality, not current cash returns. Prob-weighted IV ~$221 sits ~39% below the $361 price; even the optimistic $325 case is below market. Cross-check: at the implied current multiple TPL prices in many years of sustained 15-20%+ owner-FCF growth, which exceeds the disciplined base path. Conclusion: business quality is elite (fortress balance sheet, ~77% operating margins, ~43% ROIC), but the share price already discounts strong execution and surface/data-center optionality — limited margin of safety at $361. Stock-split note: ~0.069B post-split shares (3-for-1 from the pre-split ~23M count) reconcile $24.91B mkt cap / $361.11.
method_notes: 10-year owner-earnings DCF. Owner FCF base = reported FCF $498.3M − 100% SBC $13.8M = $484.5M (FY2025). WACC = Rf 4.3% (UST 10Y) + ERP 5.0% x beta 0.85 = 8.55%, rounded to 8.5%; TPL carries a net-cash balance sheet (only ~$18M debt, ~$248M cash, fully undrawn $500M revolver) so WACC = cost of equity, no debt weighting and no geopolitical adjustment (US-domiciled). Phase 1 (yrs 1-5): explicit owner-FCF CAGR by scenario (8%/13%/18%) reflecting Permian royalty volume growth, water-services expansion and surface monetization, holding owner-FCF margin ~stable near 60%. Phase 2 (yrs 6-10): CAGR declines linearly toward normalization. Terminal value via Gordon growth on Yr10 owner FCF with g = 2.5%/3.0%/3.5% (wide economic moat: irreplaceable West Texas surface + royalty acreage, zero capital intensity, ~43% ROIC). Flows and terminal value discounted at 8.5%; equity value = EV − net debt (net debt is −$0.23B, i.e. net cash added back); IV/share = equity / 0.069B diluted shares. Probabilities 0.375/0.475/0.15 sum to ~1.0. Inputs verified from TPL IR Q4/FY2025 and Q1 2026 press releases and stockanalysis.com (price/shares); share count cross-checked via SEC 8-K / Macrotrends confirming post-split ~68.94M shares.
